validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed. The Erbil-Duhok gas pipeline is real and was inaugurated (completed, first gas delivered) on 2025-10-28 by KRG PM Masrour Barzani: 198 km, USD 591 million, built by KAR Group, feeding the new 1,000 MW Kwashe power station in Semel district, Duhok, under the Runaki 24-hour-electricity program. Independently reported by Shafaq News, Kurdistan24 and The New Region (separate outlets, own event coverage with distinct quotes), plus KRG statements. Earlier independent trace: Iraq Oil Report (Feb 2022) reported the 52-inch Dohuk line under a KAR EPC signed December 2021 with implementation already begun. The sheet's own cited Status ref (shafaq.com Khor Mor targeting piece) is HTTP 404; the wiki's single Rudaw Arabic citation (rudawarabia.net/arabic/business/08022022) is live and DOES name the 52-inch Erbil-Duhok line, the KRG-KAR agreement (Jan 2021) and the Duhok power station, so the row was never GEM-only. CLASSIFICATION: correct - natural gas transmission trunkline (52 in / ~198 km, Khor Mor gas onward from Erbil to Duhok, ending ~35 km from the Turkish border with future export potential per Iraq Oil Report and Rudaw). DUPLICATE CHECK vs 16-row roster: P4047 Khormor-Erbil (36 in, separate EPC) is the distinct upstream segment of the same KRG corridor - different diameter, different endpoints; not a duplicate. No other roster row overlaps. Caveats: FuelSource typo/attribution and length/route discrepancy flagged separately; capacity not found in any independent source, left blank.
